intro: BACnet (Building Automation and Control Networks) is the common language of building automation: heating, cooling, lighting and meters. Every device holds objects, such as an analog input (a measured number), a binary output (an on/off command) or a schedule. Every object has properties, such as its present value. On an IP network, BACnet travels in UDP datagrams, single packets sent without a connection, to port 47808. Devices find each other by broadcast: one message that every device on the network hears.
plain: This is the common language that the machines of a building use to talk to each other: heating, air conditioning, lights and electricity meters. Each device is described as a set of labeled boxes, such as "room temperature" or "fan on or off". Other devices can read or change what is in those boxes. A control computer can ask the whole building who is there, read a meter, set a limit, and ask to be told when a value changes.

discover.title: Find the device
discover.text: The BMS (building management system, the operators' computer) knows the controller by its device number, 2001, but not by its IP address. It broadcasts Who-Is, a question to every device: is device 2001 there? Only device 2001 answers, with I-Am. The BMS takes the controller's IP address from that packet.

read.title: Read the meter
read.text: The BMS reads the present-value of analog-input 1: the building's power at the main meter. The answer is a REAL, a decimal number in 4 bytes: 268.5 kW.

write.title: Set a limit
write.text: The operator lowers the demand limit, the most power the building may draw, to 250 kW. A value that can be commanded has a priority array: 16 slots, with slot 1 the most important. The most important slot that holds a value wins. This write carries priority 8, so the value goes into slot 8.

subscribe.title: Subscribe to changes
subscribe.text: Instead of reading again and again, the BMS subscribes to COV (change of value). It asks the controller to report every change of the meter value, for one hour.

cov.title: Power drops
cov.text: The building is above the limit, so the controller sheds load: it switches off a chiller stage, part of the cooling plant. Power falls to 243.5 kW. The COV increment is the smallest change worth reporting, here 5 kW. This change is larger, so the controller tells the BMS.

frames.read: What is the present value of analog-input 1?
frames.subscribe: Tell me when analog-input 1 changes, for 3600 s

bvlc-type.name: BVLC type
bvlc-type.note: 0x81: BACnet/IP. The BVLC header comes first in every datagram.

bvlc-broadcast.name: Original-Broadcast-NPDU
bvlc-broadcast.note: 0x0B: sent to the subnet's broadcast address, 10.0.5.255. Every BACnet device on the subnet hears it.

len14.name: Length
len14.note: 14 bytes: the whole datagram, with this header.

npdu-version.name: NPDU version
npdu-version.note: The network layer header starts here. Its version is always 0x01.

npdu-plain.name: NPDU control
npdu-plain.note: 0x00: no network addresses, so the message stays on this subnet. No answer is expected.

npdu-reply.name: NPDU control
npdu-reply.note: 0x04: an answer is expected. No network addresses.

unconfirmed.name: Unconfirmed-Request
unconfirmed.note: 0x10: PDU type 1, in the high 4 bits. Nobody acknowledges it.

low-limit.name: Low limit
low-limit.note: Context tag 0, 2 bytes: 0x07D1 = 2001, the lowest device number that should answer.

high-limit.name: High limit
high-limit.note: Context tag 1: 2001 again. Only device 2001 answers. The air handler controller (AHU), device 2002, stays silent.

device-id.name: Device
device-id.note: Application tag 12 (an object identifier), 4 bytes: device 2001. The anatomy below takes it apart.

max-apdu.name: Max APDU
max-apdu.note: Unsigned, 2 bytes: it accepts messages up to 1476 bytes.

segmentation.name: Segmentation
segmentation.note: Enumerated, 1 byte: 3 = no segmentation. A message cannot be cut into pieces, so it must fit in one datagram.

vendor.name: Vendor ID
vendor.note: Unsigned: vendor 4000. ASHRAE gives each maker a number; this one is made up.

confirmed.name: Confirmed-Request
confirmed.note: 0x00: PDU type 0, in one piece. It must be answered.

max-resp.name: Max response
max-resp.note: Code 5: the BMS accepts answers up to 1476 bytes.

invoke1.name: Invoke ID 1
invoke1.note: A number the BMS picks. The answer carries it back.

invoke1-ack.name: Invoke ID 1
invoke1-ack.note: The same number as the request: this is its answer.

read-property-ack.name: ReadProperty
read-property-ack.note: Service 12: the answer to a ReadProperty.

obj-ai1.name: Object
obj-ai1.note: Context tag 0, 4 bytes: analog-input, instance 1. The main meter's power.

complex-ack.name: ComplexACK
complex-ack.note: 0x30: PDU type 3, an answer that carries data.

real-268.name: REAL
real-268.note: Application tag 4, 4 bytes: 268.5 (kW), most significant byte first.

invoke2.name: Invoke ID 2
invoke2.note: The next number the BMS picks.

obj-av1.name: Object
obj-av1.note: Context tag 0: analog-value, instance 1, the demand limit setting. 0x00800001: object type 2 in the high 10 bits.

priority8.name: Priority 8
priority8.note: Context tag 4: write into slot 8 of 16, the operator's slot. The lowest slot number that holds a value wins.

invoke3.name: Invoke ID 3
invoke3.note: The third request of the BMS.

subscribe-cov.name: SubscribeCOV
subscribe-cov.note: Service 5. COV means change of value.

process.name: Process ID 1
process.note: Context tag 0: a number the BMS picks for this subscription. Every notification carries it.

unconfirmed-notifications.name: Confirmed?
unconfirmed-notifications.note: Context tag 2, FALSE: send unconfirmed notifications, which need no answer.

lifetime.name: Lifetime
lifetime.note: Context tag 3, 0x0E10 = 3600 s. The subscription ends after one hour unless the BMS renews it.

monitored-ai1.name: Object
monitored-ai1.note: Context tag 2: the change is in analog-input 1.

remaining.name: Time remaining
remaining.note: Context tag 3, 0x0DD4 = 3540 s of the subscription left.

open4.name: Opening tag 4
open4.note: The list of values starts here.

status-flags.name: Status flags
status-flags.note: A bit string of 4 flags: in alarm, fault, overridden, out of service. All are 0: the value is normal.

t-number.name: Tag number 1
t-number.note: The high 4 bits. Its meaning depends on its place in the service: here, the property.

t-class.name: Context
t-class.note: 1: a context tag, numbered by its place. 0 would be an application tag, which names a type, such as 4 for REAL.

t-length.name: Length 1
t-length.note: One byte of value follows. 5 means a length byte follows; 6 and 7 open and close a list, as 0x3E and 0x3F do.

o-type.name: Object type 8
o-type.note: The high 10 bits: 8 is device. 0 is analog-input, 2 is analog-value.

o-instance.name: Instance 2001
o-instance.note: The low 22 bits: the object's number. A device number must be unique on the whole BACnet network.

facts.between: Workstations, controllers and field devices of a building
facts.security: None in BACnet/IP. BACnet/SC adds TLS over WebSockets

tips: A device number must be unique on the whole BACnet network, not only on one subnet. Two devices with the same number confuse every workstation.
Broadcasts do not cross IP routers. Each subnet needs a BBMD (a broadcast relay), or the device must register with one as a foreign device.
A write without a priority goes to slot 16, the lowest. If a higher slot holds a value, the write seems to do nothing.
To release a command, write NULL at the same priority. If nobody does, the slot keeps its value for good.

anatomy.tag: One tag byte, bit by bit: 0x19

playground.file: The controller's objects, as a configuration tool might export them (a made-up format). Find where each value shows up in the bytes.
playground.encoder: BACnet sends a REAL most significant byte first (ABCD). Type a value to see its bytes.
playground.device-instance: The device number. Who-Is asks for it, and I-Am answers with it.
playground.port: UDP 47808, 0xBAC0 in hex. All devices of one BACnet/IP network use the same port.
playground.segmentation: No segmentation: each answer must fit in one datagram of up to 1476 bytes.
playground.ai: An analog-input: a value the controller measures, here from the main meter.
playground.present-value: Property 85, the one ReadProperty asks for in step 2.
playground.units: Property units: 48 means kilowatts. The REAL itself carries no unit.
playground.cov-increment: A change smaller than 5 kW sends no notification.
playground.av: An analog-value: a value inside the controller, here the demand limit. It can be written.
playground.priority-array: 16 slots, slot 1 the highest. All empty, so the present value is the relinquish default. After step 3, slot 8 holds 250.0.
playground.relinquish: The value used when every slot of the priority array is empty.
